label: copy-phase input s that is the 1st or 2nd original token being fed back (recall 1-2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input is the letter s at recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the model has just echoed orig(0)=s or orig(1)=s. Magnitude is set by position: recall_idx 1 (s as first original token, input right after <DEL>) gives strong activations (~0.85-1.0 of max) and carries 83% of the mass with precision 1.0; recall_idx 2 (s as second original token) gives weak activations (~0.04-0.26 of max). Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, never on s fed back at recall_idx >= 3, and never on any other token. Output token and later context have no clear effect. Most false positives are recall_idx 2 cases in short sequences (L=3-4) where it stays silent.

issues: The false positives follow a pattern, but the explanation already says so. On the test split, s at recall_idx 2 fires 0% of the time when L=3 (precision 0.002), about 46% when L=4 (precision 0.46), and almost always when L>=5 (precision 0.9995). The label itself does not mention length, so it slightly overclaims for recall_idx 2.
Missed activations are negligible noise: 2 test steps (s at recall_idx 3, activations 0.01-0.02), holding 0.0% of the activation mass.

The other claims check out on test. The feature is active only in the copy phase and only on input s. recall_idx 1 alone gives precision 1.0 with 83% of the mass; recall_idx 2 carries 17% of the mass.

A tighter predicate that requires L>=5 for recall_idx 2 raises test F1 from 0.973 to 0.981 (precision 0.9998, recall 0.963, mass recall 0.997). The variant with L>=4 scores test F1 0.979. Both are small gains.
